rows.label: Concept
rows.text: In solids, discrete atomic energy levels broaden into energy bands. Valence band (highest occupied at 0 K), conduction band (above, where electrons conduct), and band gap E_g (forbidden region between them). Band structure determines metal/semiconductor/insulator classification.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Band gap: E_g = E_conduction_bottom - E_valence_top
Number of states in band: ~2N (from N atoms, 2 electrons per state)
Fermi-Dirac: f(E) = 1/(exp((E-E_F)/k_BT) + 1)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Isolated Atom Limit: Discrete levels only for isolated atoms. Bands form only when atoms are close (interatomic interaction).  ·  Temperature Effect: At T > 0, electrons can be thermally excited across band gap if k_BT is comparable to E_g.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Statement 1: In solids, discrete atomic energy levels broaden into energy bands due to interatomic interaction.  ·  Statement 2: The valence band is the highest energy band occupied by electrons at 0 K.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Sodium: 3s band half-filled → metal (one valence electron per atom, band holds 2).  ·  Diamond: valence band full, gap 5.5 eV → insulator.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Thinking bands are like atomic levels: Bands contain N closely spaced levels, not one level.  ·  Believing valence electrons are the only ones in valence band: Core electrons also in bands but too tightly bound to conduct.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Atomic Energy Levels: An isolated atom has discrete energy levels (1s, 2s, 2p, etc.). Electrons occupy these levels according to Pauli exclusion principle.  ·  Formation of Energy Bands: When N atoms come together to form a solid, their wavefunctions overlap. Each atomic level splits into N closely spaced levels, forming an energy band. For macroscopic N (~10²³), levels form quasi-continuous bands.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Metal: valence band partially filled or overlaps conduction band.  ·  Insulator: full valence band, large gap (> 3 eV), empty conduction band.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: Q1. Explain qualitatively how energy bands form in solids from atomic energy levels.  ·  Q2. Distinguish between valence band and conduction band.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: NEB frequently asks for qualitative explanation of band formation and classification.  ·  Distinguish valence band, conduction band, and band gap clearly.

rows.text: Energy bands — structure classified · Band | Occupation | Role · Valence | Filled | Bound electrons · Gap | Forbidden | Width decides behaviour · Conduction | Empty/partial | Carriers move

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Isolated atoms have discrete levels; solids have energy bands.  ·  N atomic levels split into N closely spaced levels forming a band.  ·  Valence band: highest occupied band at 0 K.  ·  Conduction band: band above valence band where electrons conduct.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Band theory was developed by Bloch (1928), Wilson (1931), and Peierls using quantum mechanics.  ·  The band gap of silicon (1.1 eV) corresponds to infrared wavelength (~1.1 μm) — Si is opaque to visible but transparent to IR.

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: Silicon: valence band full, gap 1.1 eV → semiconductor.  ·  Magnesium: 3s band overlaps 3p band → metal despite even valence electrons.

rows.text: Energy bands form in solids because: → B  ·  The valence band is: → B

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: Valence Band: The highest energy band containing electrons at 0 K. It may be fully or partially filled. Electrons in this band are bound to atoms.  ·  Conduction Band: The next higher energy band, typically empty or partially filled at 0 K. Electrons here are free to move and conduct electricity.  ·  Band Gap (E_g): The energy gap between valence band and conduction band where no electron states exist. Size determines electrical classification.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Thermal energy at 300 K: k_BT ≈ 0.026 eV  ·  Macroscopic Solid: Band concept requires large N — small clusters have discrete levels (quantum dots).  ·  Band gap E_g: forbidden energy region between valence and conduction bands.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Band structure determines whether solid is metal, insulator, or semiconductor.  ·  Confusing band gap with work function: Band gap is internal to material; work function is energy to remove electron from surface to vacuum.  ·  Thinking all electrons in conduction band conduct: Only electrons near Fermi level participate significantly.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Believing bands exist in isolated atoms: Bands require interatomic overlap in solids.  ·  Band gap determines conductivity: metals (no gap or overlap), semiconductors (small gap ~1 eV), insulators (large gap > 3 eV).  ·  Fermi level E_F is the energy at which occupation probability is 1/2 at T = 0 K.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Only electrons near Fermi level participate in conduction — deep band electrons are too tightly bound.  ·  Temperature excites electrons across gap if thermal energy k_BT is sufficient.  ·  Statement 3: The conduction band is the band above the valence band where electrons can move freely.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Statement 4: The band gap E_g is the forbidden energy region between valence and conduction bands.  ·  Statement 5: Electrical classification (metal/insulator/semiconductor) depends on band structure and E_g.  ·  Semiconductor: full valence band, small gap (~1 eV), some thermal excitation.
